context.exploration_scope: Generalized S7's single-goal actionability judgment to all real execution units across the 4 production goals, using the full existing convention (owner_domain + explicitly_not_executed_this_phase/why_not_executed gating), not a new rule

problem: S7 established DEFERRED for one goal's infrastructure-owned action, but it was unverified whether that was the only real blocker in the system, or whether some OTHER internal (non-infrastructure) execution unit was actually sitting genuinely executable and simply never checked.

decision.decision_summary: Judged 3 real execution units: goal_ghibli_production_pipeline=NOT_PENDING_ALREADY_RESOLVED, goal_production_runtime=DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_INFRASTRUCTURE, goal_semantic_quality=DEFERRED_EXPLICIT_SCOPE_GATE. Internally actionable: 0. No candidate generated -- none genuinely executable within this automation's boundary. External infrastructure dependency (goal_production_runtime) preserved DEFERRED: true. 0 new rule/score invented, 0 automatic execution, 0 forced bypass.

action.action_summary: Re-examined every real execution_unit on the 4 production goals' trace chains against the full existing owner_domain + explicit-gating convention; generated a candidate only for a genuinely executable internal unit if one existed; preserved all external/gated units as DEFERRED.

result.note: Every real execution unit is either already resolved, externally infrastructure-blocked, or explicitly scope-gated -- 0 forced/invented candidates.

cause.root_cause_summary: An execution boundary is only meaningfully verified once every real candidate action in the system has been checked against it, not just the one action a prior phase happened to select -- this phase closes that gap by checking all of them.

lesson: Owner-domain alone (infrastructure vs. not) is not the complete existing convention for what this automation may execute -- an internal action can still be explicitly gated (requiring a separately-scoped future phase or explicit user authorization), and honoring that gate is as much a part of the real execution boundary as the infrastructure/code distinction is.
